key_insight: Rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent design of printable bone-scaffold microstructures and their spatial placement to meet mechanical targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports highly porous, mechanically constrained implants and could extend to topology–microstructure co-design for metal additive manufacturing.
method: Generate periodic lattice unit cells with a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize cell geometries and spatial assignments under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: All eight rabbit-benchmark refinements achieved under 1% maximum relative error across six target moduli; human femoral designs reached 63% cortical porosity with compliance within 2% of its constraint and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational benchmarks, not physical fabrication or biological validation of the scaffolds.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
